lessons.title: Protecting the environment in our community
lessons.programRef: Cameroon anglophone secondary Citizenship Education syllabus, Form 2 — to be checked against the official text
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Define environment and name its parts
Explain why we must protect the environment
Describe what pupils and communities can do
reviewNotes: Teacher to verify local environmental laws and waste-collection systems in the school's area; the lesson is general and conservative.

Draft for teacher review: content is general and non-political; legal ages, institutions, names of laws and any health or road-safety statement must be verified (by a teacher, and for health topics by a health worker) before release.

blocks.md: The **environment** is everything around us: air, water, soil, plants, animals, buildings and people. We depend on it for food, water, air, shelter, medicine and income. Environmental problems in many Cameroonian communities include **waste and plastic litter**, **blocked drains and floods**, **polluted streams and wells**, **cutting of trees**, **bush burning**, **soil erosion** and **noise and smoke** from vehicles and burning.

blocks.caption: The three Rs
blocks.alt: Four boxes showing reduce, reuse, recycle and a cleaner community.

blocks.title: Causes and effects
blocks.md:
- **Waste dumped in streets**: blocks drains, causes floods, breeds flies and mosquitoes and spreads disease.
- **Cutting trees** without replanting: erosion, loss of shade, less rain and loss of animal homes.
- **Bush burning**: destroys soil life, causes smoke and can burn farms and houses.
- **Polluted water**: causes diarrhoea, typhoid and other diseases.

blocks.title: What we can do
blocks.md: Put waste in bins or approved dumps; **reduce, reuse and recycle** (reuse bottles and bags, avoid single-use plastic); plant and care for trees; keep drains clear; protect streams; avoid bush burning; use water carefully; and join clean-up days, school clubs and tree-planting campaigns. Councils should collect waste and enforce rules, and everyone should obey them.

Why protect the environment? It keeps people **healthy**, protects **farms and food supply**, preserves **wildlife** and beauty, and ensures that **future generations** will have resources. Protecting the environment is both a **right** (to a healthy environment) and a **duty** of every citizen. Small daily acts, repeated by many people, make a great difference.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Burning rubbish is not a good solution: it pollutes the air and may release toxic fumes.
- Planting a tree is good, but trees must also be watered and protected.
- Environmental protection is not only the government's job: it is the duty of everybody.

blocks.title: Example 1: cause and effect
blocks.statement: Rubbish is thrown into a roadside drain in Douala. What may happen in the rainy season?
steps: Floods may result and breed disease.
blocks.answer: The drain blocks and flooding may follow.

blocks.title: Example 2: reduce, reuse, recycle
blocks.statement: Give an example of each: reduce, reuse, recycle.
steps: Reuse: refill a bottle with water.
Recycle: give plastic to a collection point.
blocks.answer: Fewer bags; refill bottles; collect for recycling.

lessons.title: Road safety for pedestrians, cyclists and passengers
lessons.programRef: Cameroon anglophone secondary Citizenship Education syllabus, Form 2 — to be checked against the official text
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Describe safe behaviour for pedestrians and passengers
Identify common road signs and signals
Explain the danger of motorbike travel without a helmet and of speeding
Explain what to do after an accident
reviewNotes: Health and safety content to be verified against the current Highway Code of Cameroon (helmet and seat-belt rules, sign shapes and colours, penalties); first-aid advice is minimal and must be reviewed by a trained instructor.

Draft for teacher review: content is general and non-political; legal ages, institutions, names of laws and any health or road-safety statement must be verified (by a teacher, and for health topics by a health worker) before release.

blocks.md: Road accidents injure and kill many people, especially children and young people. Most accidents can be prevented. **Pedestrians** should walk on the pavement or, where there is none, on the side facing traffic; use **pedestrian crossings**; look **left, right and left again** before crossing; never cross while using a phone or playing; and wear light-coloured clothing or reflective items at night.

blocks.caption: Three kinds of road signs (simple drawings)
blocks.alt: A red octagon STOP sign, a yellow warning triangle and a blue circular sign.

blocks.title: Passengers and riders
blocks.md: Always wear a **seat belt** in a car. On a motorbike (including taxis) the rider and passenger should wear a **crash helmet**: it greatly reduces head injuries. Do not travel in an **overloaded** vehicle, in a vehicle with a **drunk or reckless** driver, or on the roof or step of a vehicle. Cyclists should keep to the side, use lights at night and obey signals.

blocks.title: Road signs
blocks.md: **Regulatory signs** (usually round, with a red edge) forbid or command something, such as **'Stop'** (octagon), **speed limit** or **no entry**. **Warning signs** (usually triangular, with a red border) warn of danger ahead, such as a school, a bend or a junction. **Information signs** (often blue or rectangular) give directions and services. **Traffic lights**: red means stop, amber means prepare to stop, green means go when it is safe.

**After an accident:** stay calm, make the scene safe, call for help from the police or emergency services, and do not move seriously injured people unless there is danger such as fire. Do what you can to help, such as stopping bleeding with clean cloth, but leave medical care to trained people. Be honest when giving information. Laws set penalties for drunk driving, speeding and driving without a licence or insurance.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Do not run across the road: look first, then walk.
- A helmet must be worn properly (fastened); a loose helmet gives little protection.
- Do not argue that 'a short trip is safe': many accidents happen near home.

blocks.title: Example 1: crossing
blocks.statement: List the steps for crossing a busy road safely.
steps: Stop at the kerb and look left, right and left again.
Use a crossing if there is one.
Cross when clear, walking and watching.
blocks.answer: Stop, look left-right-left, use a crossing, cross when clear.

blocks.title: Example 2: motorbike taxi
blocks.statement: Why should a passenger on a motorbike taxi wear a helmet?
blocks.answer: To protect the head and reduce serious injury.
